subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Prosocial Spending
description: A quick, practical guide to Prosocial Spending.

hook.text: People given $20 to spend on others reported more happiness than those told to spend it on themselves.

buildup.text: Dunn's research across 130 countries found that prosocial spending — giving to others — consistently boosts wellbeing.

discovery.text: The effect is stronger when giving feels voluntary, connected to someone, and you can see the impact of your generosity.

twist.text: The joy of giving diminishes if it's obligatory. Forced donations or guilt-driven charity don't produce the same.

climax.text: Set a small recurring amount for giving. Pick causes you care about. The happiness compounds.

punchline.text: Spend on others. It's the best investment in happiness.

quiz.question: What makes prosocial spending increase happiness?
options: Voluntary giving with visible impact boosts wellbeing
Mandatory giving produces the strongest effect
